Hi Ben — thanks for sending. Quick responses from our side: 

- Liability: we appreciate the compromise language proposal. Our legal counsel wants a clearer definition of "excluded categories" and a cap tied to fees for processor liability, not unlimited.

- SCCs vs localization: Novum prefers SCCs + a transfer impact addendum for now; localization would require a separate review and is not feasible for this timeline. We can accept SCCs provided we get audit rights over subprocessor onboarding and a 30-day notification window for changes.

We attached our marker edits in DocTrack (see link below) and one suggested tweak to Section 7 (processor obligations). Happy to review Laura's proposed language if you send it across.

Ben / Karthik — see proposed language below. Kept it short to reduce back-and-forth with Novum's counsel. I also attached a tracked-redline (OrderForm_ScheduleA_Redline.docx).

Suggested insert (Order Form / DPA):
- Processor Liability: "Except to the extent caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, Redwood's aggregate liability arising out of or related to processing of Customer Data under this Order Form shall be limited to the amounts paid by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim. This limitation shall not apply to (i) Customer's indemnity claims related to Redwood's breach of intellectual property rights, or (ii) claims arising from Redwood's intentional data exfiltration.

- Subprocessor & Audit Scope: "Redwood will provide Customer 30 days' advance notice of any new Subprocessor. Upon reasonable written request, Redwood will provide evidence of Subprocessor compliance (attestation reports, SOC or equivalent). Where Customer's legitimate compliance obligations require, Redwood will permit a single annual on-site or remote audit on agreed scope and confidentiality terms; Redwood reserves the right to require use of a mutually agreed third-party auditor and reasonable cost-sharing if audit scope exceeds standard compliance checks."

- SCCs & Transfer Addendum: "Where data transfer from the EEA is necessary, the parties agree to execute the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (as adopted) together with a mutually acceptable transfer impact addendum. The parties acknowledge SCCs as the primary mechanism; localization obligations will be addressed only where otherwise required by applicable law and subject to a separate amendment."

This preserves our limited liability model but gives Novum attestation + a narrow audit path. If you want a different cap (6 vs 12 months) say so — procurement will push on cost exposure.

—Laura

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround. Laura's proposed language (pasted below) narrows the asks and keeps the cap tied to fees. Can you confirm whether Novum can accept this form?

Quick summary of changes we propose to Novum: 
- Liability cap: 12 months' fees (exclusions for IP/intentional exfiltration)
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days + attestation reports (SOC/ISO) by default; one annual audit by third-party on agreed scope with cost-share if beyond routine checks
- SCCs: accept SCCs + transfer addendum as primary mechanism; localization only if law requires

We need a yes/no on the audit scope (attestation only vs audit with access) and the cap by EOD 2027-05-06 to keep the onboarding timeline. If you prefer, we can set up a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize.

Thanks — Ben

Ben / Team — Novum can accept the liability cap language as proposed (12 months' fees) provided we retain two clarifications: (1) audit rights must include the ability to review the subprocessor onboarding checklist and any written remediation plans arising from attestation findings; and (2) we require a commitment to notify Novum within 5 business days of any confirmed data incidents involving a subprocessor that materially affect Novum data.

We are fine with SCCs + transfer addendum as the primary transfer mechanism. On the subprocessor list: procurement asks for a one-off CSV of current Subprocessors (to be attached to the Order Form) and quarterly updates thereafter.

Attachments: Novum_DPA_comments_final.docx

If Redwood can accept the two clarifications above I'll route to procurement for final signoff and DocuSign. Prefer to keep the final execution next week.

Regards,
